_method.story: Round one analysed 20 shortlisted engineers and picked Gilbert09, webjunkie, pauldambra, Piccirello and haacked. An independent audit then re-checked every input against the raw PR data and found that the shortlist had missed strong engineers (eli-r-ph and MattBro were added), a quality rate whose numerator and denominator used different PR sets, self-repair that the follow-up-fix metric could not see, and explanations that claimed more than the merged PRs show. We fixed the quality calculation, added self-repair and human versus AI-only approval counts, rewrote the claims to match what merged, and had two independent decisions, head-to-head comparisons and a devil's-advocate pass re-rank all 22 candidates. The top three held; rafaeelaudibert entered at 4th, haacked stayed 5th after beating Piccirello head-to-head in both presentation orders, and Piccirello fell to 6th.

changes_vs_round1.reason: Both round-two decisions placed him in their top five (4th and 5th), and he beat Piccirello head-to-head in both presentation orders.
Ranked 6th by both decisions; moved into 5th after beating Piccirello head-to-head in both presentation orders and passing every gate.
Lost head-to-head to haacked and to rafaeelaudibert, each in both presentation orders.
Added after the audit found the shortlist had missed him; 32 major episodes, tied third of 22.
Added after the audit; judged on the same standard as everyone else.
Re-ranked by the round-two decisions (9th and 8th).
Second decision ranked him 12th, so he failed the gate requiring a top-7 place in both decisions.
Both decisions ranked him 10th; lost head-to-head to pauldambra in both orders.
Dropped out of the top ten after eli-r-ph was added and the decisions were re-run.

Gilbert09.headline: Warehouse-sources owner who also built PostHog's integrations credential platform
Gilbert09.why: Gilbert09 merged 2,939 PRs in the window, and 130 of his work episodes contain a major-tier PR, 3.5x the next candidate's 37. Most of that major work is on the shared warehouse sync pipeline, such as the claim-query fix after every V3 loader pod stopped loading batches for 30 minutes (#110610) and the end of duplicate rows from unfinished append runs (#113196). He also built an integrations SDK and moved the call sites of 21 products onto it (#125029), as groundwork for a separate credentials service.
keypoints: 130 major episodes, 3.5x the next candidate
Fixed a fleet-wide loader stall and duplicate rows
SDK call sites migrated across 21 products
Gilbert09.key_facts_note: Major episodes group related PRs; about 119 remain after removing roughly 870 templated add-source and add-table PRs.
caveats: His August change later caused a two-hour credential-read outage, fixed by #122385
1,575 of his 2,939 PRs were approved only by an AI bot
The SDK migration merged in late October; no quality signal yet

webjunkie.headline: Developer-experience engineer who builds shared webhook, CI and ownership plumbing
webjunkie.why: webjunkie created posthog/ingress, one inbound-webhook transport, and moved webhooks from eight providers onto it (#100292). When the Slack move exposed a path where a failed write still answered success, he made ingress return a retry status so providers redeliver (#101508). He also squashed old Django migrations so a fresh database migrates in about 5 minutes instead of about 20 (#91646).
keypoints: One webhook transport now serves eight providers
Fresh-database migrations cut from ~20 to ~5 minutes
One shared reader for code-ownership files
webjunkie.key_facts_note: trust_rank is approval-network centrality; his 24 change requests on 22 PRs show resolution by proxy, not proven adoption.
caveats: His dashboard-latency fix (#104208) reversed a regression from his own granian bump
213 of his 559 PRs were approved only by an AI bot
1000-row API list cap (#126411) merged too late to judge

pauldambra.headline: Frontend-platform engineer cutting boot cost and hardening shared Django paths
pauldambra.why: pauldambra moved the esbuild chunk map out of the HTML document into a static file, shrinking the built document from 544 KB to 10 KB (#94059). On the backend he changed refresh-token reuse handling after an OAuth incident in which /oauth/token p95 latency exceeded 300 seconds (#83929). He also stopped settings PATCH requests from wiping server-managed integration and widget-token state (#108163).
keypoints: HTML document shrank from 544 KB to 10 KB
Fixed OAuth incident and integration-state loss bugs
CI check now blocks new upward frontend imports
pauldambra.key_facts_note: The 544 KB to 10 KB figure is the built template size reported in #94059, not a measured page-load change.
caveats: Quality rate 0.952, third lowest of 22; 13 peer follow-up fixes
365 of his 652 PRs were approved only by an AI bot
ORM default change across 275 models merged November 2; untested

rafaeelaudibert.headline: Growth-team engineer whose major work centres on OAuth and MCP security
rafaeelaudibert.why: rafaeelaudibert required client authentication on the ID-JAG jwt-bearer grant, so holding an ID-JAG is no longer enough to get a PostHog token (#113013). He then linked ID-JAG identities by IdP subject instead of email, closing a path where a reassigned address reached a departed employee's account (#113014). He also removed per-account data from advertised MCP prompts, which hosts cache and serve across customers (#105547).
keypoints: Closed ID-JAG client and identity-linking gaps
Removed account data from cached MCP prompts
Highest betweenness in the review graph
rafaeelaudibert.key_facts_note: The security share of his 26 major PRs comes from the analyst's reading, not an automatic label.
caveats: Quality rate 0.945, second lowest of 22; 7 peer follow-up fixes
86 PRs had one teammate as the only human approver
hog CLI port merged late October; posthog-cli not yet retired

haacked.headline: Feature-flags engineer who led the flag_evaluations storage migration
haacked.why: haacked built the path that lets an organization stop writing $feature_flag_called to the events table: ingestion skips that copy for organizations in FLAG_EVALUATIONS_ONLY mode (#110254). HogQL queries that ask events for flag calls now read flag_evaluations instead, within limits such as an 89-day lower time bound and query shapes it refuses with an error (#124397). He also made filtered deletion requests reach flag rows that have no events copy (#117395).
keypoints: Flag calls can leave the events table
Deletion requests now reach the new table
15 engineers requested his review, third of 22
haacked.key_facts_note: Only 6 PRs carry AI co-author trailers, but 40 descriptions mention AI or agent help; trailers undercount AI use.
caveats: Mode 2 is enabled per organization by staff (#106290)
Rewrite needed four of his own major fixes after October 20
Ranked 6th by both decisions; 5th after beating Piccirello head-to-head

Piccirello.headline: Application-security engineer hardening permissions, warehouse connections and CSP
Piccirello.why: Piccirello replaced hand-copied project-access precedence with one rule that API checks, User.teams and all_users_with_access share (#114423). He took the app's Content Security Policy from report-only to enforced, extending enforcement to shared and embedded documents while the bare /exporter document stays report-only (#116719). In the eMudhra CA response his Node bump crash-looped the MCP server, adboio pinned it back, and his #122294 moved it forward again.
keypoints: 37 major episodes, second of 22
One precedence rule for project access
Staged CSP from report-only to enforced
Piccirello.key_facts_note: Merge records show the CA fixes; which services were actually redeployed is not in the data.
caveats: CA incident credit is shared with adboio, who pinned MCP back (#121721)
About 24 CSP PRs repaired or relaxed the policy (analyst count)
Team leverage 350, third lowest of 22
Piccirello.why_not_top5: He lost head-to-head to haacked in both presentation orders: haacked led on delivery (697 vs 527), quality rate (0.980 vs 0.966) and team leverage (821 vs 350).

eli-r-ph.headline: Data-correctness engineer for the persons store and capture rate limiter
eli-r-ph.why: eli-r-ph built persons_dedup, a command to clear about 782k duplicate person rows that blocked a planned UNIQUE (team_id, uuid) index (#81532). He stopped hand-run person tools from hard-deleting live rows or writing ClickHouse tombstones that Postgres never sees (#111380). In capture he fixed the global rate limiter dropping count updates on busy pods (#116680).
keypoints: 32 major episodes, tied third of 22
Person dedup, deletion and consistency tooling
Capture rate-limiter accuracy and failure handling
eli-r-ph.key_facts_note: Added in round two after the audit found the shortlist had missed him.
caveats: Repair commands merged; no evidence they ran in production
16 of his PRs were later repaired by himself
Review sought by only 3 engineers
eli-r-ph.why_not_top5: Both decisions ranked him 7th, behind haacked, whose work crosses more teams and whose review is sought by 15 engineers versus his 3.

TueHaulund.headline: Lead builder of Replay Vision, including its billing and privacy plumbing
TueHaulund.why: TueHaulund made Replay Vision's organization credit limit exact at admission, so concurrent scanners can no longer spend past it (#116148). In one September week he closed paths where a deleted recording's data survived, such as making every export of a deleted recording expire (#101932). He also restored scanner read metering in prod US and EU after an earlier change of his own had broken it (#86160).
keypoints: Exact credit-limit admission for Replay Vision
Deleted recordings' exports and derived data removed
Quality rate 0.993, best of the top ten
caveats: His own #84098 broke prod read metering for about a day
Impact stays mostly inside one product
111 of his 238 PRs were approved only by an AI bot
TueHaulund.why_not_top5: The decisions ranked him 9th and 8th: his impact stays mostly inside one product, and eli-r-ph's 32 versus 23 major episodes touch data every product reads.

mayteio.headline: Workflows engineer moving PostHog's own transactional email onto Workflows
mayteio.why: mayteio built the path for PostHog's own transactional emails to send through Workflows instead of Customer.io: #122019 routed password_reset behind a flag for one production test, and #122502 mapped the other 35 templates. He also made cyclotron job counters saturate at all 13 increment sites, so one row can no longer take its queue down (#97591).
keypoints: Transactional email path built behind a flag
Queue counters can no longer stall CDP jobs
Fixed realtime cohorts marked ready with zero members
caveats: Full cutover from Customer.io is not visible in the window
Quality rate 0.957; 1 revert and 6 peer follow-up fixes
Most email work merged in October, with little quality signal
mayteio.why_not_top5: He beat rafaeelaudibert head-to-head in both orders, but the two decisions ranked him 8th and 12th, so he failed the top-7-in-both gate.

tatoalo.headline: Leading builder of the cloud agent Tasks product and its sandboxes
tatoalo.why: tatoalo keeps long cloud task runs from losing work: sandbox snapshot rotation now preserves active worktrees (#109870), and checkpointing keeps pending messages and workspace files (#116932). He also made cloud Pi sessions treat cloud checkouts as untrusted, so repository-defined startup resources do not load there (#120934).
keypoints: Sandbox rotation preserves live worktrees
Checkpoints keep pending messages and files
Cloud checkouts treated as untrusted
caveats: Rotation launch (#86676) was followed by six of his own follow-up PRs
7 of his PRs were later fixed by peers
Impact stays inside the Tasks product
tatoalo.why_not_top5: He lost head-to-head to pauldambra in both orders: similar major episodes (21 vs 20) but about half the delivery estimate (719 vs 1,405), and fixes contained in one product.
